```{r}
HiV_data -> df
```


## Data Cleaning, Feature Engineering and Basics Statistics

```{r echo=FALSE, fig.height=7, fig.width=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, out.width="100%"}

# Rename for convenience
df <- HiV_data

# Handle Missing YEAR Values
df <- df %>%
  tidyr::fill(YEAR)

# Data Cleaning and Feature Engineering

df <- df %>%
  tidyr::fill(YEAR) %>%                                   # fill down missing YEARs
  mutate(
    Month = str_trim(Month),                       # Remove leading/trailing spaces
    Month = str_to_upper(Month),                   # Convert month names to uppercase
    Month_num = match(Month, toupper(month.abb)),  
    date = make_date(YEAR, Month_num, 1)           # Create full date variable (YYYY-MM-DD)
  )


# Summarize HIV Prevalence by Year
df_sum <- df %>%
  group_by(YEAR) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(prevalence, na.rm = TRUE)) 

# Identify the year with the highest total
max_year <- df_sum %>%
  filter(total == max(total)) %>%
  pull(YEAR)

```

## Long Short-Term Memory Modeling

```{r}
# --- Reproducibility ---
set.seed(123)
tensorflow::tf$random$set_seed(123)

# --- 0) Data: ensure date is Date and sorted monthly ---
stopifnot(all(c("YEAR","Month","prevalence","Month_num","date") %in% names(df)))
df <- df %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  arrange(date)

# Keep only modeling columns
df <- df %>% select(date, prevalence)


# --- Ensure date column and sort ---
df <- df %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  select(date, prevalence)

stopifnot(is.numeric(df$prevalence), inherits(df$date, "Date"))


```


## Create Differenced Series - Differencing helps to make the time series stationary — good for LSTM training.
```{r}
# Anchor the original (level) series once
Series <- as.numeric(df$prevalence)


# Difference the prevalence
diffed <- diff(df$prevalence, differences = 1)


# Replace NA with 0 for first differenced value 
diffed <- c(0, diffed)

```


## Apply Your Lag Function
```{r}
lag_transform <- function(x, k = 1) {
  lagged = c(rep(NA, k), x[1:(length(x) - k)])
  DF = as.data.frame(cbind(lagged, x))
  colnames(DF) <- c(paste0("x-", k), "x")
  DF[is.na(DF)] <- 0
  return(DF)
}


supervised <- lag_transform(diffed, 1)
head(supervised)


```


## Split Dataset into Training & Testing Sets (70/30 Time-Series Split)

```{r}
## Split into train and test sets for time series

N <- nrow(supervised)              # Total observations
n <- round(N * 0.70, digits = 0)   # 70% split point

train <- supervised[1:n, ]         # First 70% as training
test  <- supervised[(n+1):N, ]     # Remaining 30% as testing


```



```{r}
# ============================================================
# ARIMA Baseline using the same 70/30 train-test split
# ============================================================

# Original prevalence series
series <- as.numeric(df$prevalence)

# Define train/test on the ORIGINAL level series
train_series <- series[1:n]
test_series  <- series[(n + 1):N]

# Fit ARIMA on training data only
arima_fit <- auto.arima(
  train_series,
  seasonal = FALSE,     # set to TRUE only if you want seasonal ARIMA
  stepwise = FALSE,
  approximation = FALSE
)

# Display fitted model
summary(arima_fit)

# Forecast over the test horizon
h <- length(test_series)
arima_fc <- forecast(arima_fit, h = h)

# Predicted values
arima_pred <- as.numeric(arima_fc$mean)

# Optional: prediction intervals
arima_lower_95 <- as.numeric(arima_fc$lower[, 2])
arima_upper_95 <- as.numeric(arima_fc$upper[, 2])

```


```{r}
# ============================================================
# ARIMA Predictions on Training Data
# ============================================================

# In-sample fitted values
arima_train_pred <- fitted(arima_fit)

# Compute training errors
arima_train_rmse <- sqrt(mean((train_series - arima_train_pred)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
arima_train_mae  <- mean(abs(train_series - arima_train_pred), na.rm = TRUE)

cat("ARIMA Train RMSE:", round(arima_train_rmse, 4), "\n")
cat("ARIMA Train MAE :", round(arima_train_mae, 4), "\n")
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Evaluation Metrics for ARIMA
# ============================================================

rmse_fun <- function(actual, pred) {
  sqrt(mean((actual - pred)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
}

mae_fun <- function(actual, pred) {
  mean(abs(actual - pred), na.rm = TRUE)
}

arima_test_rmse <- rmse_fun(test_series, arima_pred)
arima_test_mae  <- mae_fun(test_series, arima_pred)

cat("ARIMA Test RMSE:", round(arima_test_rmse, 4), "\n")
cat("ARIMA Test MAE :", round(arima_test_mae, 4), "\n")
```

```{r}
# Create date index for the test period
test_dates <- df$date[(n + 1):N]

arima_plot_df <- data.frame(
  date      = test_dates,
  observed  = test_series,
  predicted = arima_pred,
  lower_95  = arima_lower_95,
  upper_95  = arima_upper_95
)

p_arima <- ggplot(arima_plot_df, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = observed, color = "Observed"), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = observed, color = "Observed"), size = 1.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = predicted, color = "ARIMA Forecast"), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower_95, ymax = upper_95),
              alpha = 0.2, fill = "grey70") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  labs(
    title = "ARIMA Forecast vs Observed HIV Prevalence",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Prevalence",
    color = NULL
  )

p_arima
```


# diebold–mariano test
```{r}
# Forecast errors
e_lstm  <- actual_test - predictions
e_arima <- test_series - arima_pred
length(e_lstm)
length(e_arima)
```


```{r}
min_len <- min(length(e_lstm), length(e_arima))

e_lstm  <- e_lstm[1:min_len]
e_arima <- e_arima[1:min_len]
```


```{r}
dm_result <- dm.test(
  e1 = e_lstm,
  e2 = e_arima,
  alternative = "two.sided",
  h = 1,           # 1-step ahead forecasts
  power = 2        # squared error loss
)

dm_result
```
